correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern opening first runs east and then turns north. It extends beyond the southern detailed coverage of Smithsonian Map10. The small APA/FPP regional map does not distinguish all of this approach and its receiving connection. No river-source point, feeder name or uninterrupted named channel is assigned to the opening.

Within Map10's southern detailed coverage, the selected northward and northeastward line matches the directly labeled upper Pomeroon corridor. This supports the visible receiving reach, without extending the name backward over the unresolved opening.

The selected upper corridor turns east in the receiving setting downstream of the distinct western Issororo approach. Smithsonian Map10 and the expedition descriptions separate Issororo from Pomeroon; Map14 independently places the Issororo collecting corridor apart from Waini and Manawarin. The model does not select the long western Issororo approach as its opening.

The selected eastward bend follows the Pomeroon receiving corridor through the St Monica–Kabakaburi setting. The separately mapped southern Arapiaco approach and its Kurishi tributary are not selected headwaters. The source descriptions distinguish these tributaries and the Tapakuma drainage from the Pomeroon traveled between Kabakaburi and Charity.

The northeastward receiving corridor reaches the Charity setting and turns northwest toward the coast. The selected inter-fragment join lies along this same lower corridor, not at a demonstrated name change. Smithsonian Map10 includes portions obscured by collection annotations; the regional APA/FPP and PAC depictions corroborate the broad lower continuation. No exact bank, small side-channel threading or naming-transition vertex is assigned.

The field accounts distinguish forested riverbanks, wet depressions and neighboring swampland from the named tributaries. The selected mapped lower corridor remains on Pomeroon; no named lake or reservoir transit is established. Tapakuma Lake and its dam belong to a separately described tributary setting. Wetland context does not prove the unresolved opening or current tidal direction and water permanence.

The final northwestward leg reaches the Pomeroon coastal-opening setting shown by the readable cartography. PAC's regional map separately depicts the Moruca River opening farther northwest. The selected tip is treated at ordinary coastal-corridor scale, not as a surveyed official mouth, a present shoreline measurement or evidence of current navigation conditions.

correspondence.component_scope: selected headward opening and northern extension
correspondence.finding: The selected northern extension reaches beyond the channel heads depicted in the authored basin map. General discussion of northern lagoons and non-integrated drainage does not establish this chosen through-link.
Mapped northern tributaries approach the del Medio corridor, but the generalized figure does not establish the complete selected transfer into the identified middle channel.

The selected middle corridor follows the mapped del Medio branch toward Las Vaquerías and Tres Arroyos, including its intervening mapped tributary joins. The local synonym Segundo Brazo is stated in the thesis prose; no exact upstream name boundary is assigned.

The selected Tres Arroyos approach and southward connection correspond to the mapped union of del Medio, Seco and Orellano into Claromecó. The other named branches are context, not extra selected fragments.
The selected reach south of the mapped three-branch junction follows the initial labeled Claromecó corridor.

The figure establishes the lower Claromecó setting and neighboring tributaries, but does not continuously distinguish the chosen western-side lower trace and all connections toward the coastal approach. This is a source-detail gap, not a proven wrong river, an exact-bank requirement or a reason to replace the selection.

The final selected segment reaches the mapped Claromecó mouth at the Atlantic coast beside Claromecó and Dunamar. The basin map and separate authored coastal figure establish this terminal setting. Exact shoreline and present channelization are not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and southward inland-ice leg
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening, first short leg and following longer southward leg occupy the generalized Inland Ice east-southeast of Qaanaaq/Thule and north of the Camp Century context label. The original covers both parts and their join through the initial southern turn. The blue and black lines are identified by the legend as ice-surface or sub-ice thematic information; they do not establish a river.

The short westward and southward steps through the southernmost turn and the following northwestward return are entirely within the readable inland-ice mapping. All eight parts and their intermediate joins are accounted for at the source scale. No natural-river name or surveyed watercourse through this reversal is established.

The westward succession after the northwestward return, including the short successive parts and the longer westward continuation, is fully covered across generalized ice. Every stored part and intervening join remains within the contiguous original. Ice contours and thickness information do not prove surface or subglacial flow along this modeled succession.

The slight southwestward steps and subsequent longer westward legs remain in the mapped ice corridor approaching the eastern side of the exposed-rock coastal belt. The original distinguishes the ice from the neighboring bedrock outcrops and includes all twelve parts and their joins. No selected lake, reservoir or managed-channel connection is established.

The lower northwestward steps pass through the generalized ice margin toward the exposed-rock belt. Their complete succession and both bounding joins are visible in the original, which distinguishes a broad southern exposed-rock area and narrower northern outcrops from intervening ice. This terrain correspondence does not assign the selection a glacier or river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower ice passage between exposed-rock areas
correspondence.finding: The westward and northwestward lower parts occupy the narrowing mapped ice passage between the broad exposed-rock area to the south and elongated exposed-rock outcrop to the north. The original covers every selected part and all intervening joins up to the final approach. Nearby geological-unit numbers and regional place labels are not hydronyms.

correspondence.component_scope: Final part and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The final part, its last changes in direction and the actual selected ending are covered at the inner coastal indentation southeast of Qaanaaq/Thule, at the generalized historical ice and exposed-rock margin. The source accounts for the terminal setting but does not establish an ordinary river mouth, a precise named glacier or a contemporary land, ice or water assignment. The model sea-terminal label is not independent naming or mouth evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening, upper approach and Orosi–upper Reventazón corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected southern approach lies in the map's Ángeles–Cuericí network and follows toward the labelled Orosi valley. The original map has a visible discontinuity between the southern network and the northern Orosi segment. Farther downstream, the mapped valley bends through the Agua Caliente joining area and east toward the next fragment. The generalized river line does not depict the Cachí impoundment passage.
correspondence.correspondence: Partly supported; headward through-link and Cachí passage pending
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Ángeles and Cuericí are retained as provisional headward context, without an exact name-transition point or transferring either label to the whole fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Reventazón through the hydroelectric corridor and northern lowland approach
correspondence.finding: The selected fragment follows the mapped connected trunk past the Angostura area and north through the lowlands toward the historical Parismina junction. Chaves identifies the sequential hydroelectric developments and describes the Reventazón dam-to-return reach. These establish managed-river context, but do not supply geographic depiction of the selected Angostura and Reventazón reservoir through-passages.
correspondence.correspondence: River corridor supported; reservoir passages pending

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final coastal fragment and Caribbean ending
correspondence.finding: The mapped final arc continues from the historical joining area east to the Caribbean at Barra de Parismina. The actually read 2025 article reports that the Reventazón still sent water east to Barra de Parismina in 2024 while a portion turned west. Its documented Parismina diversion to Jalova is a separate course and is not substituted for this selected eastern terminal.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary historical/regional corridor scale
correspondence.name_scope_limit: No current shoreline, exclusive outlet, exact mouth vertex or fixed present-day name boundary is certified.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Ángeles–Cuericí approach to the Orosi trunk
correspondence.finding: Material pending: the original hydrological map leaves an actual visible link missing. General prose naming a southern Cuericí branch does not establish the selected through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage join from mainstem10712 to mainstem10713
correspondence.finding: The two stages occupy the same mapped Reventazón corridor near the Pejibaye approach. This boundary is an inland stage join, not a mouth. Separate reservoir-passage limitations remain.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage join from mainstem10713 to mainstem10714
correspondence.finding: Continuous eastern coastal corridor in the inspected basin map. The final stage begins near the historical joining area, and the actual sea ending is farther east.

correspondence.component_scope: Cachí, Angostura and Reventazón impoundment/managed passages
correspondence.finding: Material pending: hydroelectric sequence and the managed river-return arrangement are documented, but the actual selected reservoir crossings and connecting passages are not geographically established by the inspected generalized map or article photographs. Exact engineering details and current operations are not required or asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower wetland/coastal continuation and actual sea ending
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern coastal continuation is distinguished from the independently described northward Parismina avulsion and Jalova outlet. Ordinary corridor correspondence is supported; no presently exclusive hydraulic connection is claimed.
